corrections.source_says: Fill metric with mean pairwise cosine distance; embedding_model with OpenAI text-embedding-3-small; computed_over with all submitted ideas pooled within each task and condition, then averaged across the two tasks. This is a condition-level set measure, not a participant-only flexibility score. Uncertainty is 95% bootstrap confidence intervals resampling participants for the user-study conditions; comparisons with Scanvas receive Holm correction. The reported values are raw distances, not standardized effects.
corrections.quote: We embedded each idea’s text using OpenAI’s text-embedding-3-small model [36] and calculated the mean pairwise cosine distance among ideas within each task and condition. We then averaged this measure across the two tasks.

confirmed: Source identity and version match: Scanvas: Discovering and Developing Synergistic Opportunities in Generative Design Spaces, arXiv:2609.34062v1 [cs.HC], 28 Sep 2026; 24 PDF pages. All seven listed authors match. The checker read all 599 markdown lines, including references and Appendix 7, and checked relevant numerical passages and figures in the PDF (p. 1; pp. 23-24).

The same 12 people completed both conditions and appear in both analyzed arms; they are not 24 independent participants. Figure 5 labels 58 Scanvas ideas and 53 baseline ideas, each from 12 participants. No participant exclusions are reported (pp. 10-11, Sections 4.2-4.2.2; p. 14, Figure 5).
The described sample is seven full-time industry engineers and five engineering PhD students, all with industry experience; mean time in their current roles is 3.3 years (p. 11, Section 4.2.2).

Each main task lasted 30 minutes; the session lasted approximately 90 minutes. Both conditions used GPT-5.5, and the baseline used zero-shot expansion/combination prompts. Task, condition, and presentation order were counterbalanced (pp. 10-11, Sections 4.2.1-4.2.3).

The two user tasks and their three seed ideas match the form: cooking support for an older adult with mild cognitive decline and communicating visual artwork styles to visitors with visual impairments (p. 11, Table 2).

Composite reported statistics are exact: Scanvas M=4.93, SD=0.76; baseline M=3.99, SD=0.66; p<.001. The source specifies two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests with Holm correction. The one-line finding accurately reproduces these means, the participant count, and the idea-level comparison (p. 13, Section 5.1.2; p. 14, Figure 5).
Interestingness reported means and p-value are exact: Scanvas 5.03 versus baseline 3.89, p<.001, using the stated Holm-corrected two-sided Mann-Whitney comparisons (p. 13, Section 5.1.2).

Semantic spread numbers are exact: Scanvas, 58 ideas, 0.564, 95% CI [0.513, 0.595]; baseline, 53 ideas, 0.534, 95% CI [0.477, 0.559]. The user-study confidence intervals bootstrap participants (p. 16, Table 4).

The two blind engineering experts rate output quality, and text-embedding-3-small supplies a computed diversity score across the condition idea pools. Thus criterion_3_outcome_scored_on_output=met is supported; these outcomes go beyond self-reported creativity support (p. 12, Section 4.2.4).

Core=no and criterion_2_at_least_50_people=not_met are supported by 12 analyzed people. The study compares two AI configurations; it is not AI-only output against unassisted human output. Retain context_class=none for this screening-only small experiment while assignment remains unconfirmed; the source does not establish a randomized design or explicitly document a nonrandom assignment scheme (pp. 10-11, Sections 4.2-4.2.3; p. 14, Figure 5; creativity-codebook.md, Sections 3-4).

The PDF includes tutorial details, Scanvas-only Creativity Support Index items in Table 5, and baseline AUT-fluency correlations with idea quality and within-person gains in Table 6. These appendix analyses do not add a new randomized study or a delayed unassisted-output comparison (pp. 23-24, Appendix 7; p. 12, Section 4.2.4).
This is an original system evaluation with two studies, not a synthesis; the empty pooled-estimate list and null synthesis counts are appropriate (p. 9, Section 4; p. 10, Sections 4.1-4.2).
summary: Random assignment is unconfirmed in the 12-person counterbalanced study, which remains below the 50-person threshold. Corrections address unsupported RCT/count coding, omitted studies and outcomes, diversity-test wording, incomplete metadata, and company involvement; reported means and intervals match the PDF.
